# Research notes: will Piura's 2026 dengue deaths reach 9 or more on the CDC-MINSA dashboard by Oct 15, 2026? (compiled 2026-10-05)

The latest figure found is **7 deaths** (Diresa Piura, data to Sep 23, 2026). That is **2 short** of the 9 needed. I could not read the dashboard itself, so this comes from news reports.

## 1. The dashboard (resolution source)
- **The live figure was not checked.**
  - https://www.dge.gob.pe/sala-situacional-dengue/ redirects to https://app7.dge.gob.pe/maps/sala_metaxenica/.
  - The page loads its data with JavaScript, so fetching it returned nothing usable, and no data endpoint was found.
  - Someone needs to open it by hand: Año 2026 / DENGUE / PIURA, then read "Defunciones".
- **The best indirect check also shows 7.**
  - CDC-MINSA's breakdown at epidemiological week (SE) 36, around Sep 12, gives Piura 7 deaths.
  - National totals at that point: 55,943 cases and 67 deaths.
  - Deaths by region: San Martín 18, Lambayeque 14, Madre de Dios 8, Piura 7, Ucayali 5, and 3 each in Lima, Loreto, La Libertad and Amazonas.
  - Source: El Popular, 2026-09-21: https://elpopular.pe/actualidad/2026/09/21/dengue-se-dispara-en-peru-casos-aumentan-79-y-ya-suman-casi-56-mil-contagios-y-67-fallecidos-estas-regiones-preocupan-390432
  - So the CDC count and Diresa's count agreed at that point.
- **Some reports said 6 (probably older data).** Infobae and Andina on 2026-09-22 reported 6 deaths and 10,009 cases, with 52,395 cases and 63 deaths nationally.
  - https://www.infobae.com/peru/2026/09/22/dengue-en-piura-region-supera-los-10000-casos-y-registra-seis-muertes-en-lo-que-va-de-2026/
  - https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-piura-supera-los-10000-casos-dengue-y-llaman-a-padres-a-vacunar-a-sus-hijos-1092849.aspx
- **Deaths still under investigation ("en investigación") are unknown.** The Sep 23 report lists none.
- I did not separately review https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions. It only matters under the fallback clause, if the dashboard goes down for good.

- **Cases are still rising, which is unusual for the second half of the year:**

  - The 2026 total is about 9 times 2025's. Piura has the highest case count in Peru.
  - Piura, Morropón and Sullana provinces account for 94% of cases.
  - MINSA's Dr. García Vilela (2026-09-22): second-half cases are 10 times last year's.
  - Vaccine uptake among 10- to 20-year-olds is low: 6.9% had a first dose and 1.9% had both.

- **Timing:** all of these deaths happened before the question opened. They count, because the criteria use the cumulative 2026 total.

## 3. Base rates: Piura dengue deaths by year
- **2015:** 22 deaths, 20,043 cases.
- **2016:** 18 deaths, 7,637 cases.
- Source for 2015–2016: https://elcomercio.pe/peru/piura/piura-lucha-cuerpo-cuerpo-dengue-438387-noticia/
- **2017 (coastal El Niño year):** 37 deaths by 2017-06-29, and a final total of about 51–53 (uncertain). So about 27–30% of deaths were added after June.
- **2018–2022:** not found; probably low.
- **2023:** 148 deaths and 79,643 cases. About 130 deaths had been counted by 2023-07-29 (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/73/wr/mm7304a4.htm), so about 12–13% were added after July.
- **2024:** about 32,000 cases.
  - CDC-MINSA showed 27 deaths through SE38.
  - The Colegio Médico said 28 through SE39 (https://www.infobae.com/peru/2024/10/03/dengue-en-piura-causa-28-muertes-y-colegio-medico-pide-declarar-en-alerta-epidemiologica/).
  - The final figure was about 29 (secondary reports).
  - So only 1–2 deaths were added after about SE39.
- **2025:** 0 deaths: https://www.gob.pe/institucion/regionpiura-diresa/noticias/1224346-piura-mantiene-cero-muertes-por-dengue-y-reduce-casos-en-mas-del-97-en-2025
- **Usual pattern:**
  - In a normal year, about 0–7% of deaths are added after SE38–40. Larger late additions happen in big epidemics.
  - Revisions go both ways: deaths under investigation can be confirmed or dropped (for example, 28 → 27 → 28 → 29 in 2024).
  - 2026 does not follow this pattern: it is the second half of the year and transmission is still high and rising.
- **2026 death rate:** about 1 death per 1,600 cases. At about 1,000 cases a week, that would be roughly 0.6 deaths a week. This is a crude estimate that ignores reporting delays.

criterios: This question resolves YES if the cumulative number of confirmed dengue deaths in the Piura department (Peru) for 2026 is 9 or greater (i.e., strictly exceeds 8), according to Peru's CDC-MINSA (Centro Nacional de Epidemiología, Prevención y Control de Enfermedades) dengue situation room dashboard at https://www.dge.gob.pe/sala-situacional-dengue/ , when the figure for the Piura department is read on October 15, 2026. To read the figure, set "Año de análisis" to 2026, "Enfermedad" to DENGUE, and "Departamento" to PIURA, then take the reported number of deaths ("fallecidos"/"defunciones"). It resolves NO if the reported figure is 8 or fewer. If the dashboard shows no updated figure on October 15, the most recent cumulative 2026 figure for Piura available on that date is used.
letra_pequena: If the CDC-MINSA dashboard is permanently unavailable or no longer reports department-level dengue deaths, resolution will instead use the most recent 2026 cumulative dengue death figure for the Piura department reported by Diresa Piura or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) as of October 15, 2026. Figures are cumulative year-to-date for 2026 and provisional; later upward or downward revisions do not affect resolution once read on October 15, 2026.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** 10 days, from October 5 to the October 15 reading.

(b) **Status quo:** The latest reported count is 7, so an unchanged figure resolves **No**.

(c) **Reference class:** In Piura’s 2024 dengue season, roughly 1–2 deaths were added after late September over the *rest of the year*. But 2026 transmission is unusually high for October, so that seasonal pattern may understate the risk.

(d) **No scenario:** Cases continue to rise, but fewer than two additional deaths are confirmed and entered by October 15.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Recent infections or pending investigations result in at least two additional confirmed deaths appearing on the dashboard by then.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The deciding figure is the **cumulative 2026 Piura count visible on October 15**, not deaths that occurred specifically during these ten days. Later revisions do not count. A figure of 8 is still No; 9 is Yes.

At roughly 700–1,000 new cases a week, two more deaths are plausible, but the several-week plateau at 7 and short reporting window make No more likely.

Probability: 24%

(a) **Time left:** about 10 days. The dashboard is read on October 15, 2026. By then it will probably show data through roughly epidemiological week (SE) 39–40.

(b) **Status quo:** 7 deaths. Both Diresa Piura (Sep 23) and CDC-MINSA (SE36) report 7, and no 8th death has been reported since. That resolves NO, since 9 or more is needed.

(c) **Reference class:** how often a regional count of a slow-moving death tally rises by 2 or more within about 3 weeks of reporting.
- In 2026 Piura has added about 7 deaths over about 36 weeks, roughly 0.2 per week. The count has been flat recently.
- At current case volumes (~1,000 per week) and the observed death rate (~1 per 1,600 cases), the crude rate is about 0.6 per week. Confirmation lag and the recent flat stretch point lower.
- A reasonable expectation is about 0.5–1.2 new deaths across the roughly 2.5 weeks of new data that will be visible on Oct 15.
- Under a Poisson model, P(2 or more) is about 10–34%.
- History adds a caveat: late-season additions after SE38 have usually been small (1–2 deaths, even in 2024's larger epidemic). But 2026 is unusual because transmission is still rising.

(d) **NO scenario:** Severe cases stay rare and the dashboard on Oct 15 shows 7 or 8. Any new deaths may remain "under investigation" and not be counted yet.

(e) **YES scenario:** Rising case numbers, the more aggressive DENV-3 serotype, and low vaccination produce 2 or more confirmed deaths in late September or early October. CDC-MINSA records them before Oct 15. Alternatively, the dashboard is ahead of the news and already shows 8, so only one more death is needed.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- The dashboard counts confirmed deaths only, so deaths under investigation likely don't count.
- The dashboard may assign deaths by region of residence or of occurrence, which could differ slightly from Diresa's count.
- If the dashboard is down, the latest figure available on Oct 15 is used, which is probably 7 or 8.
- Reporting lag means deaths occurring in October will likely not be visible by Oct 15.

Probability: 18%

(a) **Time left:** 10 days, from October 5 to October 15, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** The latest reported count is 7 deaths, so an unchanged figure resolves **No**.

(c) **Reference class:** Piura has recorded roughly one dengue death per 1,600 reported cases in 2026. At the reported pace of 700–1,000 new cases per week, that suggests around one additional death over a short interval like this one—not necessarily two. Reporting delays make the estimate imprecise.

(d) **No scenario:** The count stays at 7, or only one further death is confirmed, leaving it at 8.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Continued transmission and delayed confirmation add at least two deaths to the dashboard by October 15.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The deciding number is the *cumulative confirmed 2026 Piura death figure displayed or most recently available on October 15*, not deaths that occurred by then but are confirmed later. It must reach **9**; 8 is a No.

The several-week plateau at 7 deserves weight, though the unusually high ongoing case growth leaves a meaningful chance of two additions.

Probability: 32%
